elements.quote: In this systematic review and meta-analysis
elements.reason: Explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review.

elements.quote: we assessed the clinical accuracy (sensitivity and specificity) of commercially available Ag-RDTs.
elements.reason: Provides an explicit statement of the main objective.
No mention of inclusion or exclusion criteria in the abstract evidence.

elements.quote: We systematically searched multiple databases (PubMed, Web of Science Core Collection, medRvix, bioRvix, and FIND) for publications evaluating the accuracy of Ag-RDTs for SARS-CoV-2 up until 30 April 2021.
elements.reason: Identifies information sources and last search date.

elements.quote: and rated study quality and risk of bias using the QUADAS-2 assessment tool.
elements.reason: Specifies the method for assessing risk of bias.

elements.quote: Descriptive analyses of all studies were performed, and when more than 4 studies were available, a random-effects meta-analysis was used to estimate pooled sensitivity and specificity.
elements.reason: Specifies methods for presentation and synthesis of results.

elements.quote: From a total of 14,254 articles, we included 133 analytical and clinical studies resulting in 214 clinical accuracy datasets with 112,323 samples.
elements.reason: Reports total number of included studies and samples/participants.

elements.quote: the pooled AgRDT sensitivity and specificity were 71.2% (95% CI 68.2% to 74.0%) and 98.9% (95% CI 98.6% to 99.1%), respectively.
elements.reason: Presents results for main outcomes with estimates.

elements.quote: the pooled AgRDT sensitivity and specificity were 71.2% (95% CI 68.2% to 74.0%) and 98.9% (95% CI 98.6% to 99.1%), respectively.
elements.reason: Reports summary estimates with confidence intervals from meta-analysis.

elements.quote: Sensitivity increased to 76.3% (95% CI 73.1% to 79.2%) if analysis was restricted to studies that followed the Ag-RDT manufacturers' instructions.
elements.reason: Indicates direction of effect and condition favored.

elements.quote: Concerns of bias were raised across all datasets, and financial support from the manufacturer was reported in 24.1% of datasets. Our analysis was limited by the included studies' heterogeneity in design and reporting.
elements.reason: Summarizes limitations including risk of bias and heterogeneity.
No general interpretation or implications provided in the abstract evidence.

elements.quote: Funding: The study was supported by the Ministry of Science, Research and Arts of the State of Baden-Wuerttemberg, Germany (no grant number; https://mwk.baden-wuerttemberg.de/de/startseite/) and internal funds from the Heidelberg University Hospital (no grant number; https://www.heidelberg-university-hospital.com/de/) to CMD. Further, this project was funded by United Kingdom (UK) aid from the British people (grant number: 300341-102; Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office (FCMO), former UK Department of International Development (DFID); www.gov.uk/fcdo), and supported by a grant from the World Health Organization (WHO; no grant number; https://www.who.int) and a grant from Unitaid (grant number: 2019-32-FIND MDR; https://unitaid.org) to Foundation of New Diagnostics (FIND; JAS, SC, SO, AM).
elements.reason: Specifies primary sources of funding.

elements.quote: We registered the review on PROSPERO (registration number: CRD42020225140).
elements.reason: Provides register name and registration number.

elements.quote: Weincluded studies evaluating the accuracy of commercially available Ag-RDTs to establish a diagnosis of SARS-CoV-2 infection, against reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) or cell culture as reference standard. We included all study populations irrespective of age, presence of symptoms, or study location. We considered cohort studies, nested cohort studies, case-control or cross-sectional studies, and randomized studies.
elements.reason: Specifies study designs, populations, settings, and reference standard.

elements.quote: We included both peer-reviewed publications and preprints.
elements.reason: Publication status is specified, but language and dissemination year are not explicitly stated in the eligibility criteria.
The review does not exclude studies based on outcomes not measured, only on reporting or other criteria, so distinction is not applicable.

elements.quote: Wedifferentiated between clinical accuracy studies (performed on clinical samples) and analytical accuracy studies (performed on spiked samples with a known quantity of virus). ... we only considered data from clinical accuracy studies as eligible for the meta-analysis. Separately, we summarized the results of analytical studies...
elements.reason: Specifies groups for synthesis (clinical vs analytical accuracy studies) and links to meta-analysis eligibility.

elements.quote: Although the size threshold of 10 is arbitrary, such small studies are more likely to give unreliable estimates of sensitivity and specificity.
elements.reason: Provides rationale for the restriction on study size.

elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly describes the predefined subgroups and criteria for meta-analysis, indicating the process for deciding study eligibility for each synthesis.

elements.quote: We extracted raw data from the studies and recalculated performance estimates where possible based on the extracted data. In an effort to use as much of the heterogeneous data as possible, the cutoffs for the Ct value groups were relaxed by 2-3 points within each range.
elements.reason: The text explicitly describes data extraction, recalculation of estimates to handle incomplete data, and data conversions (e.g., adjusting Ct value cutoffs) for subgroup analysis, covering methods to prepare data for synthesis.

elements.quote: Two types of sensitivity analyses were planned: estimation of sensitivity and specificity excluding case-control studies, and estimation of sensitivity and specificity excluding nonpeer-reviewed studies. elements.quote: Values differ from those provided in the respective paper due to missing or contradictory data.
elements.reason: The manuscript identifies that some results were computed or estimated rather than directly reported.

No evidence found in retrieved chunks that briefly summarises relevant characteristics and risk of bias for each synthesis (e.g., per Ag-RDT meta-analysis). Overall summaries are provided, but not broken down by synthesis.

No evidence found in retrieved chunks that identifies the studies contributing to each synthesis (e.g., lists of studies for specific Ag-RDT meta-analyses). References to supplementary materials like S3 Fig are not sufficient without explicit data.

elements.quote: Based on 119 datasets with 71,424 tests performed, we were able to perform bivariate meta-analysis of the sensitivity and specificity for 12 different Ag-RDTs... Three Ag-RDTs did not have sufficient data to allow for a bivariate meta-analysis, so a univariate analysis was conducted... The remaining 35 Ag-RDTs did not present sufficient data for univariate or bivariate meta-analysis. However, 9/35 had results presented in more than 1 dataset, and these are summarized in Table 2.
elements.reason: The manuscript reports results for all statistical syntheses conducted, including bivariate and univariate meta-analyses, and descriptive summaries for tests with insufficient data.

elements.quote: pooled sensitivity and specificity were 72.1% (95% CI 68.8% to 75.3%) and 99.0% (95% CI 98.7% to 99.2%)
elements.reason: For each meta-analysis, summary estimates (sensitivity and specificity) and their precision (95% confidence intervals) are reported.
No quantitative measures of statistical heterogeneity (e.g., I² or tau²) are reported in the text for the meta-analyses.

elements.quote: For the INNOVA SARS-CoV-2 Antigen Rapid Qualitative Test... this resulted in a pooled sensitivity and specificity of 76.1% (95% CI 68.1% to 84.1%) and 99.4% (95% CI 98.7% to 100%)... The remaining 35 Ag-RDTs... summarized in Table 2 with sensitivity ranges such as 8.1% to 80.7%.
elements.reason: For univariate analysis and descriptive syntheses, synthesized results are reported with precision (confidence intervals) or equivalent information (ranges).

elements.quote: Herein, the widest ranges of sensitivity were found for the ESPLINE SARS-CoV-2... with sensitivity reported between 8.1% and 80.7%... Overall, the lowest sensitivity range was reported for the SARS-CoV-2 Antigen Rapid Test by MEDsan: 36.5% to 45.2%.
elements.reason: For descriptive syntheses without effect estimates, relevant statistics (ranges) and a question-consistent interpretation (e.g., comparative performance) are reported.

elements.quote: In one of these, the Rapid COVID-19 Ag Test by Healgen (sensitivity 77.1%) performed better than Standard Q and Panbio (sensitivity 69.8% and 67.7%, respectively).
elements.reason: When groups are compared (e.g., different tests), the direction of effect (e.g., 'performed better') is described.
